item.title: Show HN: Bowerbird, a private image organizer for Windows, Mac and Linux (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description: A few months ago I started building a small tool for myself. I had folders full of images and wanted a fast way to browse, tag and rate them without uploading anything or signing up for anything. Think Eagle (which I use) but for images you already have. I've decided to launch it as a desktop app. It's called Bowerbird. It's now out for Windows, Mac and Linux. * Open any folder and see every image inside, including subfolders * You can rate and tag images * You can search and filter, and save those queries as smart folders * Your images stay where they are: no account or cloud * The app only connects to check for updates and licenses * You only pay once, no subscription * There's a free 14 days trial It's still early days so it's on discount for a couple of weeks. item.title: Show HN: Free tool to collect invoices and spot forgotten subscriptions (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description: At my previous company, I spent hours every month going through our bank statements and looking for the invoice behind each charge. There are many invoice collectors, with varying accuracy, but AI makes this much better now. I also noticed that while checking the statements, I was subconsciously reviewing the tools we pay for. So I built a free tool that works exactly how I wanted it to. It combines invoice collection with spotting forgotten subscriptions and duplicates, alerts for price rises and renewals, and some nifty actions, like drafting an email to ask for a discount. Many times it works, you just need to ask. It's fully free, but limited to reading 100 invoices a month, since I cover the AI costs and make no money from it. I also want to release a self-hosted version, where you could use your own models, including local ones. The code needs some cleanup and refactoring first, so I'll do it if people actually use this (I set the goal at 100 users). Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50641746 Points: 3 # Comments: 0

item.title: Launch HN: Versine (YC F26) - MCP to send and receive money (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description: Hey HN, we're Harshith, Param, and Vishnu and we're building Versine (https://versine.com). Versine lets you send and request money just by talking or texting with your AI (think Venmo with an MCP). We're software engineers who have worked on distributed systems at Stripe, Databricks, and Amazon. Versine is an MCP that sits in front of a wallet with a balance. With it, your agent can do things like: - Send money to someone with your approval (via passkey in our app) - Send and request money to/from up to 100 people at once - Send money to people without a Versine account (they cash out to their bank in 2 mins) - Pay people without your explicit approval to trusted contacts (you can set this) Here's a demo: https://youtube.com/shorts/Q9X7zioEqi0 We started working on this because assistants are frustratingly hands-off when it comes to finance and money movement. You can have your assistant go through a receipt and map out all the amounts owed taking care of splitting the subtotal, taxes, tips, but at the end of it the assistant hands back work to you when you have to go out and make the Venmo transfer. Our current solution is oriented towards power users: those who want to automate everything through their agent use us to split dinners, group trips, or settle poker ledgers. We see ourselves unlocking more value for the general consumer as 1. More people turn into power users of agents, and 2. We expand to a more complete banking solution: deposits, transfers, wires, everything you can (and more) do with your bank offered as an MCP. Behind the scenes, each user has a self-custodial stablecoin wallet storing USDC on Base. With self-custodial wallets, users own their keys, meaning money can't be sent without their approval. Interestingly, we were almost forced into this solution because we had around 4 weeks to build this product (after a pivot), and traditional fiat with a partner bank would have caused far too many regulatory and compliance slowdowns. Because of that, the only fast option that remained was using stablecoin wallets. It also ensures we aren't a Money Services Business (MSB) since we don't hold control or access to the user's funds. Each call to the wallet creates what we call one-time or recurring standing permissions. For a one-time payment, your agent makes an MCP call, and you receive a notification in our mobile app. Once you swipe up in the app and approve with a passkey (or your device's biometric method), we create a one-time permission that instructs your wallet to send $X to your recipient's address. Trusted contacts let your agent send money to people that you've previously authorized without explicit passkey approval. Generally, these are people that you'd trust to send your money back even if your agent made a mistake. We're also able to support sending money to someone off Versine using claim forwarding, where the user authorizes us to forward a specific amount to a future address (which we create once we verify a recipient's OTP). Param worked on scaling vector search at Databricks and harness evals at Glean. Harshith worked on core Stripe Connect fee-processing infrastructure and built an AWS Fargate autoscaler at Amazon. Vishnu worked on intent-based agent testing infrastructure at Amazon. None of us were experienced in stablecoin or crypto infra before working on Versine but our distributed systems experience has helped us a lot. We'd love for you guys to try it! It's available on iOS and Android and as an MCP on ChatGPT and Claude. We also support a public MCP and REST API for other agents. Please let us know how you find it and if it works as you'd hoped! https://versine.com Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50634426 Points: 93 # Comments: 87
